metadata.summary: Being at Old Trafford on Tuesday night was quite incredible.
metadata.content: Manchester United reporter notebook: Shea Lacey and Old Trafford young guns offer Michael Carrick hope of unlikely revival | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Manchester United reporter notebook: Shea Lacey and Old Trafford young guns offer Michael Carrick hope of unlikely revival Shea Lacey's impressive cameo against Roma offered Michael Carrick fresh hope of an unlikely Manchester United revival; the 19-year-old's impact underlined why the academy graduate deserves a starting role against Aston Villa as Carrick considers putting his faith in youth Danyal Khan Sky Sports News Reporter @DanyalHKhan Sunday 8 November 2026 08:44, UK Being at Old Trafford on Tuesday night was quite incredible. Whether the feeling proves short-lived or sparks something bigger for Michael Carrick and Manchester United remains to be seen, but it was important to see a stadium that has been starved of moments to celebrate this season roaring again. There was plenty to dissect from the comeback win over Roma , but one of the biggest positives for Carrick was the impressive 15-minute cameo from 19-year-old Shea Lacey. Lacey came on with the drive, confidence and quality to take responsibility and push United forward. His inch-perfect pass to Matheus Cunha was pivotal in setting up the winner. metadata.summary: Chris Billam-Smith finished the fight on his feet, shaking his head in protest, when referee Lee Every halted him in the seventh round against Cheavon Clarke.
metadata.content: Dana White: Chris Billam-Smith stopped too soon in shock defeat to Cheavon Clarke | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Dana White: Chris Billam-Smith stopped too soon in shock defeat to Cheavon Clarke Zuffa Boxing promoter Dana White thought Chris Billam-Smith was stopped too early; Cheavon Clarke halted Billam-Smith in the seventh round of their fight at the Copper Box Arena in London; "If he was blocking the shots he wouldn't have been dancing," Clarke said Sunday 8 November 2026 07:12, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Zuffa Boxing 12 cruiserweight main event between Chev Clarke and Chris Billam-Smith Chris Billam-Smith finished the fight on his feet, shaking his head in protest, when referee Lee Every halted him in the seventh round against Cheavon Clarke. No one before had seen Billam-Smith in that kind of predicament. He'd never previously been dropped let alone stopped. But Cheavon had put him down twice in that round before finishing matters against an old amateur rival . Billam-Smith wanted to carry on and Zuffa Boxing promoter Dana White agreed, saying: "I thought it was early." But he added: "Only CBS can answer that question." Clarke backed the referee's call, convinced he had the former WBO world champion in severe distress . "If he was blocking the shots he wouldn't have been dancing," Clarke said. messages.text: Norris claims Sao Paulo GP pole

metadata.summary: Lando Norris claimed pole position after a hugely-challenging Sao Paulo Grand Prix qualifying in treacherous wet conditions, for a race that will see Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen start at the back of the grid.
metadata.content: Sao Paulo GP Qualifying: Lando Norris claims rain-hit pole in wild conditions with Lewis Hamilton, Max Verstappen to start at back | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Sao Paulo GP Qualifying: Lando Norris claims rain-hit pole in wild conditions with Lewis Hamilton, Max Verstappen to start at back Lando Norris tames awful wet conditions for his third Brazil pole in a row; Frustrated Russell drops down from second with grid penalty; Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen starting 20th and 21st; watch Sunday's Sao Paulo GP live at 5pm on Sky Sports F1, build-up from 3.30pm By James Galloway at Interlagos Sunday 8 November 2026 07:54, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from qualifying for the 2026 Grand Prix. Lando Norris claimed pole position after a hugely-challenging Sao Paulo Grand Prix qualifying in treacherous wet conditions, for a race that will see Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen start at the back of the grid. On a rain-hit day at ever-unpredictable Interlagos, qualifying was suspended for over an hour and 20 minutes after a torrential downpour hit the drivers' first laps of Q1. The rain eventually eased - but never particularly stopped - to allow running to take place, creating a thrilling and unpredictable battle for pole. messages.text: Ali and Nicolson on a collision course?

metadata.summary: Ramla Ali and Skye Nicolson could meet in a unification contest early next year if they both win their title fights, live on Sky Sports in the early hours of Monday morning.
metadata.content: Ramla Ali and Skye Nicolson could be on a collision course if they win their world title fights in Texas | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Ramla Ali and Skye Nicolson could be on a collision course if they win their world title fights in Texas Ramla Ali's extraordinary story has already been made into a film, but she has the chance to become a two-belt world champion in Texas, while Skye Nicolson eyes a fight with the winner of her bout; Watch Alycia Baumgardner vs Elif Nur Turhan live on Sky Sports from 1.30am John Dennen Sports Journalist @johndennen Sunday 8 November 2026 08:42, UK Image: Ramla Ali fights live on Sky Sports in the early hours of Monday morning. Ramla Ali and Skye Nicolson could meet in a unification contest early next year if they both win their title fights, live on Sky Sports in the early hours of Monday morning. At College Park Center in Arlington, Ali takes on Mikiah Kreps for the IBF and WBO super-bantamweight titles, while Nicolson, the WBC champion at super-bantam, boxes Miyo Yoshida on the same bill. Ali is looking for another fairytale moment in her journey through boxing. A refugee from Somalia, she moved to London when she was a child. She took up boxing, initially in secret, and eventually became the first woman to box for Somalia at an Olympic Games. messages.text: 'Very disappointed' Russell says Mercedes error cost him Sao Paulo GP pole

metadata.summary: George Russell said he was "really disappointed" as he insisted a "misjudgement" by his Mercedes team had cost him pole position for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.
metadata.content: George Russell: 'Very disappointed' Mercedes driver says team error cost him Sao Paulo GP pole in chaotic wet qualifying | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content George Russell: 'Very disappointed' Mercedes driver says team error cost him Sao Paulo GP pole in chaotic wet qualifying George Russell was beaten to pole for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix by Lando Norris; Russell believes Mercedes' instruction for him to abort a flying lap cost him pole; watch Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix live at 5pm on Sky Sports F1, build-up from 3.30pm Sunday 8 November 2026 07:43, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell was seething after being told to back off at a time when he believed he could have pushed for P1 during the Q3 session in Sao Paulo George Russell said he was "really disappointed" as he insisted a "misjudgement" by his Mercedes team had cost him pole position for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix. Russell drove impressively throughout a hugely-challenging wet qualifying session at Interlagos but ultimately missed out on pole position by two tenths to McLaren's Lando Norris. The Mercedes driver had led Norris by four tenths of a second after their first runs in Q3, but was then told to abort his second run when he was being held up by the Williams of Alex Albon. messages.text: Clarke claims stunning upset win over Billam-Smith

metadata.summary: Cheavon Clarke scored a stunning stoppage win over Chris Billam-Smith at the Copper Box Arena in London.
metadata.content: Cheavon Clarke hands Chris Billam-Smith first stoppage loss in stunning upset win over former world champion | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Cheavon Clarke hands Chris Billam-Smith first stoppage loss in stunning upset win over former world champion Cheavon Clarke beat former world champion Chris Billam-Smith at the Copper Box Arena in London; Billam-Smith had never been dropped before but Clarke put him over twice before the referee halted the Bournemouth star John Dennen Sports Journalist @johndennen Sunday 8 November 2026 07:53, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Zuffa Boxing 12 cruiserweight main event between Chev Clarke and Chris Billam-Smith and Chev Clarke Cheavon Clarke scored a stunning stoppage win over Chris Billam-Smith at the Copper Box Arena in London. He not only knocked the former world champion down for the first time in Billam-Smith's career, he put him over twice and handed the Bournemouth star a first stoppage defeat. Halted on the ropes, as Clarke's right hooks streaked in, Billam-Smith at once shook his head to protest as the referee waved it off. Clarke, after a thrilling win over Jack Massey last time out, was looking for a big-name scalp that would launch him into the top class of the division. He got it.
